timeScale._midPageNote: Composer asked (2026-08-20): half a page at 2 cm/beat, the rest at 1.5? Not supported today (xOfSeconds is linear per view), BUT it is a contained extension, not a rebuild: because ONLY coords.js computes pixels, a piecewise-linear time map in the view would re-space layout, cursor, and animated objects automatically. If ever wanted: break scale only at chunk boundaries and mark the seam visually — in proportional notation distance IS time, so an unmarked scale change silently mis-calibrates the reader. The cursor also visibly changes speed at the seam. Held as a MARKED DOOR: build only when a real page demands it.

verticalBudget._status: DECIDED 2026-08-20: option A — accept, machinery handles actual collisions (composer: 'A should be fine, chances are there won't be too many collisions')
verticalBudget._finding: Every part spans F#1–F4 (T1/T8 to G4). Fixed furniture fits (tags 4.8 ss, dynamics 5.9 ss vs 6.51 budget). Tops: G4 ink ≈ 7.0 ss — lands in the inter-lane gap, OK. BOTTOMS: F#1 head+ledger+staccato dot ≈ 7.7 ss ≈ 9 px past the lane edge — through the 4 px gap and ~5 px into the neighbor's band. Systemic (all ten parts carry the range), but an actual COLLISION needs both neighbors at opposite extremes at the same x — expected occasional, exactly what the protrusion detector + overrides exist for.
verticalBudget._fixLadder: Per-collision options at tier 3, in preference order, all data: (1) flip furniture to the free side — accents/dynamics above instead of below (engraving override); (2) horizontal micro-nudge dxSs a few px (kept sub-perceptual — proportional distance is meaning); (3) per-PAGE lane rebalance — weights are per view, give the crowded part a few px on that page only; (4) octave device (8vb) for ledger towers (tier-2 vocabulary); (5) per-page staff size — mechanically trivial (a page is a view) but reads as a zoom jump, last resort; (6) the global C-switch.
verticalBudget._cSwitch: TESTED 2026-08-20 (proofs E-staff31p6 vs E-staff28): staff size flipped as ONE number on the chosen no-header container — identical ink inventory (335/173/162/22 elements), staff span lands at exactly 31.60 vs 28.00 px measured off the drawn lines, text scales within 0.1% of the predicted ratio. At staff 28 the F#1 worst case drops to ~2.5 px past the lane edge = inside the gap, no neighbor contact — so if collisions ever annoy, the one-number switch to ~28 clears them wholesale.

EARLIER: day 23 (composer: yes to 'the ladder, the named dynamics, ppp to fff, and the velocity conversion'): THE ONE-SHOT DYNAMIC = one marking from five WIDE bands, middle collapsed (ppp · p · mf · f · fff), looked up from the event's captured velocity (IR `vel`, amendment 5). Device dynMark 'band' resolves here; a literal mark (e.g. 'sfzp') bypasses the table.
layout._chainAboveGapNote: day 23: when the chain sits ABOVE a flagged stem-up unit it goes BETWEEN the staff and the flag (composer: 'let's see if we can get the dynamic above the staff and below the bottom of the flag'); the flag-clear stem rule then clears the chain, and this tighter gap (vs the 0.45 house standard) is the air on each side of the mark in that slot.
layout._breathNote: day 23 (composer, corrected the same hour): THE BAR ENDS A BREATH BEFORE THE NEXT GESTURE — 'working backwards... the next gesture minus breath'. The measured sample length only CAPS it, so a note with room keeps its full ring (nothing earlier in the piece is affected) and only a note crowded by the next attack is shortened. 0.5 s = a moderately quick tuba breath (snatch 0.25-0.35 s; full relaxed on a large horn 1-1.5 s). DRAWING ONLY — playback still follows the IR duration (D49), since the sample rings what it rings. flagShortBarSeconds warns when the next attack forces a bar under that length, for the composer to judge note by note; a gap shorter than the breath draws no bar at all and warns.
layout._gcImpactInsetNote: day 24: the disc's landing height in ss, mirroring animated.gc.look.impactInsetPx (and engraving.render.gc.look). Layout needs it in ss to decide whether a GC-bearing head actually reaches the disc — the push that clears it is now CONDITIONAL, because once the ball was lowered to the lane edge almost no head collides and an unconditional push drags heads off their own go time. test_animobj asserts the px and ss copies agree, converting through gcImpactRadiusSs/impactRadiusPx, the one quantity stated in both units.
layout._gcImpactRadiusNote: day 23: the GC impact marker's radius in ss — the GC look's 4 px at the 1080 frame over the jury frame's 7.9 px/ss. Both scale with frame height, so the ratio is frame-invariant. A unit carrying a GC is anchored at least this + tightGapSs before the go time, so its notehead and ledgers clear the marker (and therefore the descending arc, which only reaches head height in the last ~15 ms).

figures._note: day 24 — THE FIGURE STANDARDS AS DATA (composer: 'let's try to capture these as standards or something documented somehow because after the clear, we've lost... I've had to reestablish some of these rules'). tools/notate_section.js builds every --cluster and --beam overlay FROM these blocks, so a rule lives here once and docs/NOTATION_STANDARDS.md describes it in words. Edit here; the next extract carries it.

cluster._restsNote: day 24 (D62): a rest may not cross a beat. The composer's performance model is that a cluster is GO THEN COUNT — and since no tempo is marked on the page, the rests are the only thing that shows where the beat is. A rest BEGINNING on a beat makes it visible; one running across it hides it. Measured on T3 before the change: beats 2, 3 and 4 all fell inside a rest symbol. Dotted values remain available where they do not cross a beat.

dynamicsRule._status: CAPTURED, NOT WIRED (day 24, composer: 'forte with accents is good. We can capture that as a standard. I'm not sure we're ready for AI to generate the clusters, but let's just capture it in case that does happen'). No flag runs this; --dyn and --accents stay the composer's. It is written down so a future generator starts from the composer's own reasoning rather than re-deriving it.
rule: 1. Band every partial from its captured velocity (engraving.layout.dynamicBands).

2. AMBIENT: place one dynamic at the SOFTER level, not one per partial. Where the level shifts mid-cluster, place a second ambient at that point — in practice at a beam-group start, taking that member's own band.
3. ACCENTS: every partial whose band is ABOVE its current ambient gets an accent; partials AT the ambient get nothing.
4. The result is the ambient+deviation shape from DYNAMICS_FRAMEWORK: 'loud, slightly softer, loud, slightly softer, loud loud' is ONE f plus accents, never fff f fff f fff fff.
dynamicsRule._why: There is no engraved mark meaning 'slightly softer' (the composer asked). The inverse exists and is standard: state the soft level once, mark the loud ones. One dynamic instead of six.
dynamicsRule._validation: MEASURED against both real clusters, day 24. cl-2 (T2, 6 partials, velocities 121 105 121 109 127 127 = two bands fff/f): the rule gives ambient f + accents 1,3,5,6 — EXACTLY the composer's own choice, derived independently. cl-1 (T1, 12 partials, three bands mf/f/fff): the rule reproduces the two ambients (members 1 and 9, at the two beam-group starts) and three of four accents (4,7,8) but NOT the accent on member 12, whose band (f) is BELOW its ambient (fff) — a shaping decision on the final partial that no velocity rule predicts. So: reliable for a two-band cluster, a starting point for a three-band one, never the last word.
dynamicsRule._confidence: Do not auto-apply. A generated cluster should PROPOSE marks under this rule and say which partials it could not explain.

cluster._note: A CLUSTER (D56): a composer-named span of partials on ONE analysed tempo. Go line and GC on the FIRST partial only ('the GC only on the first one, so it launches the whole cluster'); every partial's NOTEHEAD LEFT EDGE sits on its own go time ('because of the scrolling person'); filled head at the 0.844 cell scale, staccato dot at the 0.15 tight gap; every partial written as a 16th, gaps as 16th rests one per slot (day 35, --rests16 on every new build; --restFit N the correction; tuplet-internal slot rests keep the bracket's value), the second beam level SOLID through the group's rests (day 35, --beamsThrough; --beamlets N the per-group exception; before day 35: beamlets, beamStubSs — db1 reproduces that writing from its own command). Dynamics = the ambient+deviation model (DYNAMICS_FRAMEWORK): one ambient mark on a chosen member, ACCENTS on the members louder than it — 'loud, slightly softer, loud' is f with accents, not fff f fff. Per-partial marks remain available (--dyn n,n,n).

beam._note: A BEAM (day 24): notes joined by a beam that KEEP their own technique device — no tempo, no grid, no rests. The short one-shot is the 16th (two beam levels, so the second level is a stub); anything in ringTechniques is the long note (primary beam only). NO go lines; GC on the RINGING note (day 24, composer: 'let's shift the GC to the half note' - the long note is the one whose entry needs the cue; 'first' stays legal and is the fallback when no member rings); EVERY member's HEAD is centred on its go time (first on the 16th, then on the half note once it carried the GC: 'the note head should be centered on go time along with the GC'); the members' dynamics go TOGETHER on one row ABOVE the beam, the beam lowered to fit them ('they both need to be at the top because the sfzp won't fit below').

figures._beamsAreFlat: A beam is FLAT, always — layout levels every group to the tip furthest from the staff and moves the stems with it (the group's height, never a member's: a mixed fortepiano+staccato group once sloped by half a space because each note derived the beam from its own flag). Not a number — a law in notation/lib/layout.js, restated here so it is found.

layout._ringBarGapNote: day 24 (composer: 'have the notehead and ledger and a little bit of space and then a duration bar'): the ring bar starts this far after the nh-unit's RIGHT INK EDGE — head, ledgers, accidental, whatever the unit carries — instead of at the go line. The day-22 spec said flush with the go line, which was the same thing while every unit hung before its go time; a head centred ON the go time (beam figures, day 24) put the unit on top of the bar. Default = nhGapSs 0.25, the piece's existing small horizontal gap, which makes the rule a NO-OP for every default-anchored fortepiano (there headDx + rightExt = -nhGapSs exactly).
layout._beamStubNote: day 23 (composer's midway solution): every partial is written as a 16th and the gaps carry 16th rests, but the SECOND beam level is a STUB (a fractional beam / beamlet) on a note with no 16th neighbour, and a connecting segment only between adjacent 16ths — 'a short beam where the sixteenth note beam is, not something that connects', so the phrasing still reads. Standard practice (Gould: fractional beams); length in ss, tune by eye. Stubs point RIGHT, toward the gap the note opens.
layout._tupletNote: day 23: THE COMPOSER'S OWN LILYPOND STANDARD, surveyed from piece #2's lilypond_code (809 .ly files, 101 with tuplets; TupletBracket.direction #UP 29/29, bracket-visibility ##t, padding 0.5 ('bracket height'), TupletNumber.text = tuplet-number::calc-fraction-text 29/32 — the override that prints '3:2' rather than a bare '3' — font-size -5, and the composer's own flatten-tuplet-bracket which levels both ends = the straight bracket) and MEASURED by tools/glyph_probe_tuplet.js: thickness 0.16, hook 0.7 descending toward the notes, the horizontal drawn in two segments with a 2.6388 ss gap for a 3-character numeral (hence numeralGapPerCharSs 0.88) inset 0.4, numeral baseline 0.41 BELOW the line so the digits straddle it, size 1.2348 italic. No glyph tracing: LP draws the bracket as strokes and typesets the numeral as text, so this app does the same in its own notation font.
layout._bracketOverflowNote: day 31 (composer, T7: 'brackets... are too far down. There's plenty of room above'): a repaired group's bracket goes on the HEAD side only when it fits INSIDE the lane there; otherwise it returns to the BEAM side (its engraving home) and may overflow the lane edge by up to this much — the inter-lane gap plus the neighbour's usually-empty margin. Past that (T9: 1.75 over) it stays head-side and anything colliding moves instead. The measured cases: T7 beam-side 1.25 over (goes up, per the composer) · T2 1.39 (stays head-side, approved look) · T9 1.75 (stays head-side).
layout._gapMediumNote: day 31, THE MEDIUM GAP (composer: 'there is also the smaller vertical gap which we use for the staccato dot. And there was meant to be a medium one too between the two. which we haven't come up with, but we can.'): the third tier of the vertical-gap system — 0.15 tight (dot, dyn-stem) · 0.30 MEDIUM · 0.45 standard (session-77 stack). 0.30 proposed as the midpoint, and it is the value the under-flag chain has used since day 23 as chainAboveGapSs — the medium tier existed un-named in one special case. Used by the day-31 wide-register repair pass for its row joints (approved pages never trigger it, so the classic 0.45 stacks are untouched). The parked cuivré lift (NITS day 30: 'a midway constant between tight 0.15 and the standard, then raise the marks') would take this same constant when the composer says.
layout._tightGapNote: day 23, THE TIGHT GAP STANDARD (composer): the staccato dot sits 0.15 ss (1.2 px at the jury frame) from the head's edge ('reduce 50% the gap'), and the same value is the air between a dynamic's right edge and the stem ('just a little tiny bit of gap... akin to the staccato gap'). nhDotGapSs and dynStemGapSs both carry it; one number to change if the eye wants more.
layout._seccoGapNote: PLAN 2j.2 (the composer 2026-09-16, RUNNING_LOG §540): the gap between the surge's cut edge and the 's' of 'sempre secco' = the staccato-dot gap (nhDotGapSs / dynStemGapSs, 0.15). The word sits at the cut edge's top, top-justified on the curve's top (layout.js the secco block; render.js yAt 'top').

chordColumn._chordTolNote: the extractor's CHORD_TOL (notation/lib/extract_core.js), restated for the layout: a chunk whose notes all fall within this of its first onset is drawn as ONE column at that onset (the bricks keep each note's own time). 40 ms: a played chord spreads 10-30 ms; the fastest written rhythm here is 130 ms.
chordColumn._provenance: 2026-09-11 (septet PLAN 2a.4): piece #2's LOCKED chord rules, carried with their numbers — composition_for_two_pianos_and_two_percussion/tools/notation_studio/engine/dimensions_table.json noteColumn (D.8.1, the LilyPond cluster matrix: a note within 1 staff position of the previous one flips to the other side of the column, displaced one notehead width) and accidentalColumn (D.8.2, the LilyPond accidental matrix: minLateralGap 0.10, collision tolerance 0.05; a colliding accidental takes the next full slot left). Its docs/CHORD_SPACING_RULES.md §0 names these canonical and its older constants superseded. The algorithms are notation/lib/chord_column.js, ported from its note_column.js / accidental_column.js. The gap to the notehead is glyphs.json standards.accidental.gapToNotehead (0.10, the same lock).

layout._dynStemGapNote: day 23 (composer): above a stem-up flagged unit the dynamic sits BESIDE the stem — its right edge dynStemGapSs left of the stem — not centred on the head column; the flag, on the stem's other side, keeps its full height (flagScaleY back to 1.0; the compression stays available as a knob).
layout._flagScaleYNote: day 23: vertical-only scale on the 8th flag for the staccato unit (composer: 'if we can adjust it so it's not so tall'). At 1.0 the staff + mf + flag chain (2 + 0.3 + 0.97 + 0.3 + 3.008 = 6.58 ss) overflows the 6.51 ss half-lane by 0.07; at 0.65 the flag is 1.96 ss tall and the chain tops out at 5.53. Anisotropic — the Emmentaler curl is compressed, not redrawn; alternatives (a procedural straight flag as in LilyPond's modern-straight style, or a uniform scale) are listed in RUNNING_LOG day 23.
layout._flagClearanceNote: day 23 (composer, wc-29): 'have the bottom of the flag clear the staff, just like three pixels or so — maybe not the full typical gap.' 3 px at the jury frame (7.9 px/ss) = 0.38 ss. Piece #2's computeFlaggedStemLength law with this clearance (p2 used stem.flagClearance.clearanceSs = 1.0): the flag's near edge clears the outer staff line; applied by devices with nhStemRule 'flagClear'; the default stem length wins when already longer. Head scale 0.844 = piece #2 notehead.cellMotive.scaleFactor (the composer's remembered small-notehead formulation; uniform scale on the same outline, no new glyph). nhDot = the staccato dot on the notehead side (dotYFor).
layout._chainSideNote: day 23 (composer, after the ledger measurement: F#1 ends 0.5 px above the lane edge; nothing stacks below any note at or below A1). THE SIDE-WITH-ROOM RULE: the column chain (dynamic pair / single mark; articulation and instruction when they arrive) stacks BELOW by default and flips ABOVE the unit's top ink when the chain would not fit between the note's bottom ink and the lane edge — Gould permits dynamics above where below is obstructed and articulation at the stem side when the head side is crowded. laneHalfSs = the jury frame's half-lane in ss: ((1080 - 16 - 36) / 10) / 7.9 / 2 = 6.51 (realizations.video-jury.lanes + staff 31.6); it is the PRESENTATION lane on purpose — a sparse experiment IR (capped lane) must make the same choice the draft will. An ottava, when one exists, pins the chain to its own side (the sign is outermost and cannot flip).
layout._stackNote: day 22, THE VERTICAL COLUMN STANDARD (composer decision; Gould and piece #2's own chain agree): below-staff chrome stacks notehead-outward in this order, each element stackGapSs (the session-77 0.45) past the previous outer ink. Articulation/instruction slots defined for when those elements arrive.
layout._dynPairNote: day 22, composer: NO derivation — the two marks state the bottom and top LEVELS, not the curve. This piece: every surge is full-curve ppp->fff (morph section + manual judgments via authored overrides). Another piece may change the pair here.
layout._dynArrowNote: day 22, the hairpin replacement (composer: 'this is new'): start mark centered on the note column · gapSs · arrow (lenSs total incl. headSs triangle) · gapSs · end mark. Gaps = the 0.45 house standard; thickness = stem thickness.

partLabel._septetNote: 2026-09-11 (composer: "center them on the appropriate staff, so centered on the middle staff line"): with the ensemble registry the label is centred on its staff's middle line (the grand staff: between its staves); the baseline sits baselineBelowEm × font size below the line, so the text's visual middle (Crimson's caps and figures, ~0.64 em tall) is on it. yOffsetSs is the tuba's top-of-lane placement, used without an ensemble.

glissCurve._note: day 35, the morph section (composer): the glissando is ONE smooth interpolated line per section, brightOrange (#F04B00 = piece #1's `brightOrange`, its glissando colour), taking PRECISELY the TOP HALF of the lane; the crescendo takes the bottom half. sectionHead._note: day 35, composer: the section figure is niente circle - arrow - fff, sitting UNDER the staff at the house `dynY` row 'just like all the other dynamics', ending one standard spacer before the go line. NO LilyPond niente glyph exists (checked ours and piece #1's) - in LilyPond the circled tip is DRAWN - so the circle is drawn: diameter = the measured height of the `m` in mf (0.4695 ss; mp and mf agree to the digit), stroked at the arrow's thickness, centred on the arrow's axis. The mark and arrow are ORDINARY items (glyph + dynarrow), so they are drawn by the identical code path as every other dynamic.

crescCurve._d42Note: D42: the morph crescendo takes the same standard (limeGreen, 0.3 · 2 px · 0.3). Was fill 0.22, no stroke (day 35).
